record.original_question: If H is a subgraph of G, must the maximum crossing number satisfy cr^M(H) ≤ cr^M(G), where cr^M denotes the largest possible number of pairwise edge crossings over all good drawings?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.8 If H is a subgraph of G, then cr M (H ) ≤ cr M (G).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A drawing of a finite simple graph $G$ in the plane is called good if (i) every edge is a simple arc whose endpoints are the images of its incident vertices, (ii) no edge passes through a vertex other than its endpoints, (iii) any two edges share at most one interior point, where they cross transversally, (iv) no three edges share an interior point, and (v) two edges sharing a common endpoint do not cross. For such a drawing $D$, let $\mathrm{cr}(D)$ denote the number of pairs of edges that cross. The maximum crossing number of $G$ is
$$\mathrm{cr}^{M}(G) := \max_{D} \mathrm{cr}(D),$$
where the maximum is over all good drawings $D$ of $G$ in the plane.

Prove or disprove: for every finite simple graph $G$ and every subgraph $H$ of $G$,
$$\mathrm{cr}^{M}(H) \le \mathrm{cr}^{M}(G).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The subgraph monotonicity conjecture for the maximum crossing number $\mathrm{cr}^M$ is discussed in Schaefer's survey "The Graph Crossing Number and its Variants" as an open problem; no proof or counterexample is known. Recent literature on maximum (rectilinear) crossing numbers continues to treat this question as unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Graph Crossing Number and its Variants: A Survey
status_evidence.snippet: The Subgraph Problem asks: given a graph G and a subgraph H of G, must it be true that the maximum crossing number of H is at most that of G? Listed as an unresolved monotonicity conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is stated as an open problem in Schaefer's survey on crossing number variants.

status_evidence.title: A Note on the Maximum Rectilinear Crossing Number of Spiders
status_evidence.snippet: Work on maximum (rectilinear) crossing numbers treats monotonicity-type questions as still active.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on maximum crossing numbers does not report a resolution of the subgraph monotonicity conjecture.
